newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia economic growth seen at 7.5 pct in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia economic growth seen at 7.5 pct in 1997.

text.p: Indonesian economic research group Econit predicted the country's 1997 economic growth at 7.5 percent against an expected 7.3 percent in 1996 despite likely rising political uncertainties and a slow down in exports, Bisnis Indonesia daily reported on Monday.
The government policy to cool down the economy which had started in the first semester of this year was likely to continue through the first semester of 1997, the newspaper quoted Econit as saying.
But Econit said government expenditure would rise as the elections, due in mid-1997, neared.
"The policy will provide a solid ground for the country to achieve more stable economic growth during the second semester of 1997 and throughout 1998," Econit managing director Arif Arryman said.
Indonesia's economic growth in 1995 was 8.1 percent, he said.

Econit director Rizal Ramli said if political uncertainties rose due to the scheduled general elections next year and turned into political unrest, the growth was likely to be revised down by at least 0.2 percentage points.
Arryman said Indonesia's exports were likely to slow down as the country was unlikely to be able to exploit the expected higher economic growth in developed countries.
Bisnis Indonesia did not give further details.
